FAQ

To help you select and maintain the perfect natural window treatments, we have compiled this woven wood shades guide addressing common questions about liners, humidity, care, and motorization. Review the table below for quick answers to essential planning and care considerations.

QuestionAnswer
Should I order woven wood shades with an attached blackout liner or an independent dual shade?An attached liner operates on the same control mechanism as the woven face fabric, moving up and down together as a single unit. A dual roller shade operates independently on its own roller behind the natural weave. If you want maximum daytime sunlight filtered through the reeds while retaining full room-darkening control at night, choose the independent dual liner configuration.
How do natural bamboo and grass shades perform in humid Marietta, Georgia basements or sunrooms?Natural fibers like bamboo, reeds, and grasses absorb airborne moisture, which causes stretching or mildew over time in unconditioned spaces. For damp basements or enclosed sunrooms around Marietta, Georgia, install synthetic woven materials or ensure the space maintains continuous climate control. Homes with standard HVAC dehumidification can safely support natural wood weaves without warping.
What is the best method to remove dust from textured bamboo weaves without snagging the fibers?Clean textured weaves by using the soft brush attachment on your vacuum cleaner with low suction, moving strictly horizontally along the grain of the reeds. Avoid damp rags, chemical cleaners, or saturating the fibers with water, as excess moisture damages the wood finish and causes stains. Use a feather duster or compressed air canister for tight gaps between woven slats.
Can motorized lift systems handle the weight of dense, oversized woven wood window coverings?Heavy, wide natural materials like dense timber slats or layered jute require heavy-duty motors calibrated to lift substantial weight loads. Pairing automated roller systems with custom shades eliminates manual cord strain on tall windows. If you mount wide treatments on large windows in Marietta, Georgia, dividing the expanse into two shades on a single headrail prevents motor burnout.

How to Measure Your Windows for Blinds Accurately

Accurately measuring your windows is the foundation for perfectly fitted blinds, preventing costly mistakes and ensuring a professional finish. Whether you’re opting for an inside mount (blinds fitted within the window frame) or an outside mount (blinds covering the window frame), precise measurements are essential for residents near East Marietta.

Before you begin, gather a steel tape measure, a pencil, and paper. Always measure each window individually, even if they appear to be the same size, as slight variations can lead to ill-fitting blinds. For an inside mount, measure the width at three points: top, middle, and bottom, and use the narrowest measurement. For height, measure at three points: left, middle, and right, and use the shortest measurement.

For an outside mount, decide how much overlap you want around the window frame – typically 2-4 inches on each side for width and 2-4 inches above and below for height. This overlap helps block light seepage and provides better privacy. Add these desired overlaps to your window opening measurements. For more information on choosing the right window treatments, explore our window treatments guide.

  1. Decide on Mount Type. Determine if you want an inside mount (within the window frame) or an outside mount (overlapping the window frame). This choice affects how you measure.
  2. Measure Width (Inside Mount). Measure the inside width of the window frame at the top, middle, and bottom. Record the smallest of these three measurements. This is your width.
  3. Measure Height (Inside Mount). Measure the inside height of the window frame at the left, middle, and right. Record the smallest of these three measurements. This is your height.
  4. Measure Width (Outside Mount). Measure the exact width of your window opening. Add 2-4 inches to each side (total 4-8 inches) for desired overlap. This is your width.
  5. Measure Height (Outside Mount). Measure the exact height of your window opening. Add 2-4 inches above and below (total 4-8 inches) for desired overlap. This is your height.
  6. Double-Check Measurements. Always remeasure everything at least twice to ensure accuracy. It’s better to be safe than sorry, especially when considering custom window treatments.
